title: REQUIREMENTS FOR SETTING REINSURANCE CONTACT OFFICE
text:
REPUBLIC OF GHANA
INSURANCE ACT, 2021 ACT 1061
REQUIREMENTS FOR SETTING UP REINSURANCE CONTACT OFFICE
1. A completed application form
2. A licence application fee of $25,000
3. A letter from jurisdiction regulator that applicant has a valid licence.
4. A copy of a valid licence to operate in Head Office
5. Curriculum vitae of Country/Office Manager
6. Curriculum vitae and other details of the company’s directors
7. Evidence of a bank deposit of GHS1,000,000 for the operations of the contact offices
8. A five (5) year business plan clearly showing the strategy of the contact office
CONDITIONS FOR THE MAINTENANCE AND OPERATION OF A CONTACT
OFFICE IN GHANA BY A REINSURER
1. The reinsurer shall hold at all times a deposit of an amount of USD 500,000 with an approved
Bank under lien in favour of the National Insurance Commission.
2. The reinsurer shall register with the Registrar General’s Department as an external company
doing business in Ghana.
3. The reinsurer shall engage Ghanaian nationals for their operations in line with the NIC
Corporate Governance and Risks Management Framework.
4. The reinsurer shall maintain a bank account in Ghana to allow tracking of remittances. The
account(s) will be subject to inspection by the Commission.
5. The reinsurer and the contact office will be required to file periodic returns with the
Commission as may be determined by the Commission.
6. The office should operate solely as a contact office. No business may be underwritten or
transacted by the office.

7. The contact office shall pay to the NIC, annual levy/licence fees to be determined by the NIC.
8. The reinsurer and the contact office shall comply with other conditions that may be issued by
the Commission from time to time.
9. The reinsurance company and its contact office shall comply with the Insurance Act 2021 Act
1061 and all relevant legal and regulatory directives and requirements.

title: NEW LICENSE REQUIREMENT
text:
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMMISSION
REQUIREMENTS FOR OPERATIONAL LICENCES OF INSURANCE, REINSURANCE,
INSURANCE BROKING, REINSURANCE BROKING COMPANIES, TECHNICAL SERVICE
PROVIDERS, LOSS ADJUSTERS AND LOSS ASSESSORS
Applicants can only be bodies corporate incorporated in Ghana. The application shall
be accompanied by the following;
1. Copy of Certificate of Incorporation
2. Copies of documents filed at the Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC)
showing the details of shareholding structure and the Board of Directors
3. Beneficial Ownership Profile document from the ORC
4. The details of each shareholder are as follows;
In the case of a natural person;
• Name
• Nationality
• Country of residence
• CV, completed Personal Questionnaire and Personality Notes Form
• Any other relevant information.
In the case of a body corporate,
• Name
• Nature of Business
• Company’s detailed organizational structure
• Detailed group structure (if applicable), indicating the chain of connection/showing
all associated and affiliated companies to the ultimate owners
• Country of residence
• The company’s Audited Financial Statement for the last five years and
• Any other relevant information.
5. Curriculum Vitae completed Personal Questionnaire and Personality Notes Form
from each Shareholder (in the case of public companies, only significant holders
owning 10% or more need to provide their details), Director, Principal Officers (at
least 2) and proposed Chief Finance Officer/ Finance Manager (in the case of a
Technical Service Provider).

6. A detailed 5-year Business Plan containing relevant projections (3 years for
Broking, Technical Service Providers, Loss Adjusting firms and Loss Assessors).
7. Evidence of availability of minimum required capital and its source; Reinsurance
Company GH₵125million (for each class of business), Insurance Company
GH₵50million, Reinsurance Broking Company GH₵1million, Broking/Technical
Service Providers/Loss Adjusting Companies GH₵500,000, and Loss Assessor
GH₵200,000. At least 60% of the minimum capital requirements must be in cash
or cash equivalent.
8. An audited Statement of Affairs showing all assets and liabilities (valuation
reports for motor vehicle(s), building(s) and properties with titles).
9. Proposed insurance products including proposal forms, policy wordings and rates.
10. Particulars of and letter of consent from Auditor, including the digital address of
auditors.
11. In the case of Life companies, particulars and a letter of consent from Actuary.
12. Copies of all contracts regulating the applicant’s relationship with all other
companies transferring the applicant’s functions to other companies and any
other contracts, the contents of which influence the financial situation of the
applicant.
13. The latest audited financial statement of the applicant, audited accounts of the
immediate parent and consolidated group accounts, if any.
14. A description of the location of office accommodation to be approved by the
National Insurance Commission, including the digital address and receipt of
payment of rent.
15. A non-refundable Application fee of GH₵10,000 for Technical Service
Providers/Loss Assessors, GH₵26,000 for Insurance Brokers/ Loss Adjusters,
GH₵52,000 for Reinsurance Brokers, GH₵65,000 for Insurers, GH₵97,500 for
Reinsurers and $25,000 for Foreign Reinsurers/Reinsurance Contact Office
respectively. A licence fee will be charged if the application is approved.
NOTE:
a) The application file will be closed if you fail to respond to licence application queries
after a period of four (4) months and the process will have to be restarted anew.

b) A Technical Service Provider may sell both Life and Non-Life microinsurance
products.

title: ACADEMIC VERIFICATION CONSENT FORM

EXPLANATORY NOTE FOR THE “AUTHORISATION FOR RELEASE OF
ACADEMIC RECORDS” FORM (IF APPLICABLE)
This form is a supplementary form to the Personality Notes Form and the Abridged Personality
Notes form.
Who Should Complete this Form?
It only applies to applicants or nominees who:
1. have pursued or are currently pursuing higher educational/ professional /vocational
program in a school/institution outside Ghana.
2. are in possession of academic or professional certificate(s) which were issued by an
institution outside Ghana.
What is Required When Completing the Form?
1. The form must be fully completed, signed and dated by the nominee or applicant described
above.
2. Applicant is required to indicate the full address of each school/institution attended either
at the top right corner of each completed form or next to the name of the school indicated.
3. Provide student ID number on each form.
How Many Forms Must be Completed by Applicants?
1. Each form must be addressed to each school/institution attended outside Ghana.
2. The applicant or nominee is only permitted to consolidate his/her educational history on
one form for the same school/institution if he/she pursued or is pursuing multiple
educational programs in that school/institution at different times in the said
school/institution outside Ghana. In other words, an applicant or nominee can fill one form
if multiple certificates were issued to the applicant by one school/institution.
NB:
Kindly note that applicants or nominees who are completing the Abridged Personality Notes
form are required to complete this form, purposely for newly obtained
professional/academic qualification(s) which were obtained outside Ghana, after the NIC

title: BOARD COMPOSITION FOR BROKERS LOSS ADJUSTERS
text:
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMMISSION
GUIDELINES FOR COMPOSITION OF BOARDS OF LOSS
ADJUSTERS AND BROKERS
1. The board shall have a minimum of three (3) members, including the Chief Executive officer
(CEO)
2. The role of the CEO and the Chairperson shall not be combined.
3. The Chairperson shall be a non-executive director.
4. At least 1/3rd of the total membership of the board shall be composed of independent directors.
5. The Board shall include non-executive directors of sufficient caliber and standing to provide a
balanced discussion and decision making at board meetings.
DEFINITIONS
Independent Director
An Independent Director shall be “non-executive” and shall be free from any business with the
company or its associated companies, which can interfere materially with the exercise of his/her
independent and partial judgment. He/She shall not have close family ties with any of the Company’s
Directors, Senior Management or Significant Shareholder.
Non-Executive Director
A non-executive director’ is a director who is not engaged in the daily management of the company.

title: BUSINESS PLAN FOR BROKERS
text:
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMMISSION
GUIDELINES ON THE CONTENT AND SUBMISSION OF BUSINESS PLANS SUBMITTED
BY BROKERS, LOSS ADJUSTERS AND TECHNICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS TO THE NIC
UNDER SECTION 111 OF INSURANCE ACT, 2021, ACT 1061
1.0 Introduction
Section 111 of Insurance Act, 2021 requires every insurance intermediary to submit its
application for licence to the NIC accompanied with the prescribed documentation. These
guidelines are to provide guidance on the contents of business plans required (as prescribed
documentation) to be submitted with applications for intermediary’s licence.
The guidelines shall be relevant for the following situations
1. Companies desirous of applying to the NIC for a new licence to carry on insurance
broking, loss adjusting business and technical service providers.
2. Companies specifically directed by the NIC to submit a business plan.
2.0 Summary/General Contents of Business Plans
Any business plan required to be submitted to the NIC shall contain information on the following;
(a). Describe the company’s business strategy, including marketing, and risk management
strategies
(b). Include financial projections for at least three years.
© State the assumptions which underlie the projections, the reasons for adopting those
assumptions and the accounting policies on which the projections are based.
(d) Provide detailed information on the company’s board of directors’ organisational structure,
management personnel and internal controls.
(e) Provide information on all existing, proposed and intended third party agreements.
(f) The business plan shall be signed by three directors of the company including the Chief
Executive and the Board Chairman.
3.0 Business Strategy
The information required to be contained in this section of the business plan is as follows;
3.1 Background Information
The business plan should include the following;
1 | P a ge

a. a description of the applicant
b. if the applicant is a member of a group of companies, a description of the group and the
company’s place within it, including corporate structure chart (“family tree”) with applicable
shareholdings, showing the position of the company within the group
c. the significant activities of the group
d. A description in narrative and tabular format, of the past history of the book of business.
3.2 Target market and marketing strategy
A brief description of the company’s proposed marketing strategy including the target market(s),
and a description of the proposed sources of business.
4.0 Financial Resources and Projections
A brief description of the amount, forms and sources of capital that will be available for the
business of the company.
Financial projections for each of the first three financial years following authorisation. The
projection must clearly demonstrate that the capital available will be adequate for the company’s
operations. The projections must include the following;
4.1 A forecast Revenue Account by class of business. This should
include as a minimum the following:
(a) Estimates relating to premiums or contributions both gross and net of commissions and broken
down by class of business
(b) Estimates relating to commissions, fees and other income broken down by class of business
(c) Estimates of management expenses
(d) Profit projections showing expected dividend payouts
4.2 A forecast Balance Sheet.
4.3 A forecast cash flow including cost of future capital expenditure to be undertaken
5.0 Board of Directors, Management, Personnel and Internal Controls
2 | P a ge

5.1 Board of Directors
The following information about the proposed board of the company;
(a) Composition of the board; names of members whether they are Executive or Independent
(b) Qualifications and experience of the board members
(c) Minimum number of times the board is required to meet during a year.
(d) A list of reports required to be submitted by management to the board and the frequency with
which such reports are to be submitted
Generally, the Commission will consider the collective suitability
of the board. The Commission would usually expect its composition
to be such that it is able to act independently of any controller or
parent company. The Commission considers that non-executive
directors, with appropriate experience, help to provide the
necessary skill and balance on the board.
5.2 Corporate/Organisational Structure
A corporate structure chart and a description of the
proposed apportionment of significant responsibilities between the
applicant’s management team. The structure chart should set out
the management structure, responsibilities and reporting lines.
5.3 Personnel and Internal Controls
A summary of the arrangements by which systems
and controls will be established and maintained in the
organisation, including an explanation of how these will be
overseen. The business plan should set out the capacity of the
applicant’s systems and controls to monitor and control all
significant aspects of the applicant’s operations, and should
include (but not be restricted to):
(a) details of persons responsible for prospecting, underwriting, IT and financial reporting,
including preparation of regulatory returns and compliance with relevant laws, regulations and
guidelines.
(b) staffing levels in each area/department/unit;
The applicant needs to demonstrate that adequate staff
with relevant experience are available at all levels.
6.0 Outsourcing and third party agreements
3 | P a ge

A description of any material outsourcing or subcontracting arrangements, in particular any
outsourcing of Accounting and IT functions, including:
(a) background information concerning the third party
to whom functions will be outsourced;
(b) details of functions which will be outsourced;
(c) details of those persons in the firm who will be
responsible for overseeing such delegations, including details
as to how the outsourcing will be monitored and controlled;
(d) copies of any agreements with persons who will
manage any significant part of the business of the applicant;
and
(e) copies of any agreements with insurance companies
clearly explaining any commission arrangements.
In general, the quality, skills and experience of the
management required will depend on, among
other things, the type and volume of business it expects to
undertake.
4 | P a ge

title: BOARD COMPOSITION FOR INSURERS AND REINSURERS
text:
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMMISSION
GUIDELINES FOR COMPOSITION OF BOARDS OF
INSURANCE/REINSURANCE COMPANIES
1. The board shall have a minimum of seven (7) members, including the Chief Executive
officer (CEO)
2. The role of the CEO and the Chairperson shall not be combined.
3. The Chairperson shall be a non-executive director.
4. At least two of the Board members must be Ghanaians
5. Either the Board Chairman or the Chief Executive Officer should be a Ghanaian
6. Where the Chief Executive Officer is not a Ghanaian, the Chief Finance Officer should
be a Ghanaian.
7. At least 1/3rd of the total membership of the board (subject to a minimum of two (2)
shall be composed of independent directors.
8. The Board shall include non-executive directors of sufficient caliber and standing to
provide a balanced discussion and decision making at board meetings.
9. Where a life company and a non-life company are either fully or substantially owned by
the same shareholder(s), or where one is a subsidiary of the other:
 The chairperson of the life company shall not be the chairperson of the non-life
company; or vice-versa.
 An independent director of the life company shall not be presented as an independent
director of the non-life company; or vice versa

DEFINITIONS
Independent Director
An Independent Director shall be “non-executive” and shall be free from any business with
the company or its associated companies, which can interfere materially with the exercise of
his/her independent and partial judgment. He/She shall not have close family ties with any of
the Company’s Directors, Senior Management or Significant Shareholder.
Non-Executive Director
A non-executive director’ is a director who is not engaged in the daily management of the
company.

title: EMPLOYMENT VERIFICATION CONSENT FORM
text:
EXPLANATORY NOTE FOR THE “EMPLOYMENT VERIFICATION CONSENT”
FORM (IF APPLICABLE)
This form is a supplementary form to the Personality Notes Forms and the Abridged Personality
Notes form.
Who Should Complete this Form?
It only applies to applicants or nominees who have ever worked or are working outside Ghana.
What is Required When Completing the Form?
1. The form must be fully completed, signed and dated by the nominee or applicant who have
ever worked or are currently in employment outside Ghana, either as an intern, support
staff, contract staff or full-time staff.
2. Provide Social Security Number in that foreign country on each completed form.
How Many Forms Must be Completed by Applicants?
1. A form filled must be addressed and filled for each school/institution attended outside
Ghana.
2. The applicant or nominee is only permitted to consolidate his/her employment history for
the same Company on one form if he/she has occupied multiple positions at different times
in the said Company outside Ghana.
NB:
Kindly note that applicants or nominees who are completing the Abridged Personality Notes
form are required to complete this form, purposely to provide only updated employment
history which were obtained outside Ghana, after the NIC had approved them for more than
two years.

title: ABRIDGED PERSONALITY NOTES FORM
text:
EXPLANATORY NOTES - ABRIGDED PERSONALITY NOTES FORM (AFTER TWO
(2) YEARS OF THE NIC’s APPROVAL)
Who should complete this Form?
1. The abridged form is to be completed by newly appointed Directors, Senior Managers or
Key Persons of regulated entities who have been previously approved by the National
Insurance Commission (NIC), but due to their acceptance of new appointment offers two
years after the NIC has granted them a no objection, they are required to undergo a new
vetting process.
2. Persons who occupied the Chief Executive Officers/ Managing Directors positions prior to
2017 and they have been presented again by another regulated entity for a position
specified in Section 55(1) of the Insurance Act 2021, (Act 1061).
What is the essence of this Form?
The purpose of this abridged form is for these nominees to provide any new updates regarding
the applicant that were not in existence during their initial fitness and propriety assessment
process. This includes, but not limited to, additional qualifications, changes in marital status,
additional employment history etc.

on the website for these information.

and Insurance Loss Adjuster)

…………………………………………………………………………………………………..

.………………………………………………………...........................………………………..
5. In the case of a Technical Service Provider, state
a) Name of Insurer(s) in partnership with…………………………………………………………..
b) Name of Telco(s) in partnership with ……………………………………………………………
6. State whether any of the parties connected with this application have ever applied, individually or in
conjunction with others, for authority to transact insurance or other financial services business in any
other jurisdiction and, if so, provide full details.
7. State any jurisdiction(s) outside Ghana in which the applicant carries on, or is proposing to carry
on, business as an insurance intermediary.
8. Details of professional indemnity insurance effected or to be effected, including insurer and level of
cover. (A minimum of GH¢200,000 for (Re)Insurance Broking/Loss Adjusting Companies and
GH¢500,000 for Technical Service Providers).

DECLARATION BY APPLICANT
We hereby apply for a licence and declare the above particulars to be true and correct and agree to notify the
National Insurance Commission of any material alteration to the foregoing information supplied, and that,
(a) we have not been adjudged insolvent or bankrupt
(b) we have not made any assignment or any arrangement or composition with creditors which has
been rescinded or set aside, and
(c) we have not been convicted by a court of an offence involving dishonesty, fraud or gross
misconduct, nor have had to appeal against conviction by the terms of any enactment in force in
Ghana or any other country.

For use of National Insurance Commission only

Date received:…………………. 1. Acknowledged: .. ….………….
Fee Paid:…………………… 2. Further Enquiries: ..……………..
Receipt No:…………………. 3. Decision: ..……………..
ENCLOSURES TO THE APPLICATION
1. Copies of company registration documents from the Registrar General’s Department.
2. Detailed curriculum vitae, completed Personal Questionnaire and Personality Notes Form from all
Shareholders, Directors and Principal Officers.
3. A detailed Business Plan containing estimated setting up costs and relevant projections.
4. Evidence of availability of minimum capital and its source.
5. Copies of all contracts regulating applicant’s relationship with other companies, transferring the
applicant’s functions to other companies and any other contracts the contents of which influence the
financial situation of the applicant.

6. If applicant is a company, the following must be attached.
(a) The names (including any previous name), addresses and nationalities of all persons exercising control
over the applicant, e.g. shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners of shares in the company;
(b) Where shares are beneficially owned by a corporate body, or the company is part of a group, the chain
of connection (group organization chart showing all associated and affiliated companies) to the ultimate
owners must be provided;
(c) The directors and principal officers of the applicant, showing their respective positions with the
applicant.
7. Particulars and letters of consent from the applicant’s auditor.
8. The latest Audited Statement of Affairs of the applicant.
9. Evidence of professional indemnity cover.
10. Description of the office location to be approved by the Commission.
11. Application fee.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR TECHNICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS
1. Copies of Partnership Agreements must be submitted.
2. A Technical Service Provider has the liberty to enter into partnership with unlimited number of Insurance
Companies, both life and non-life insurance companies to sell microinsurance products, subject to approval by
the NIC.
3. Applications for licensing of Sub-Agents and Trainee Agents (newly recruited agents) to sell microinsurance
products are required to be presented to the NIC by an Insurer. The licensed agent can sell for the insurer that
presented him for licensing. Meanwhile, the agent can sell for one life and one non-life insurance company. But
both companies must present the agent for licensing.
4. A Technical Service Provider, shall submit to the NIC on semi-annual basis, and in a format determined by the
NIC, a report containing the number of policies sold during the year by product type and the premiums generated.
The report shall be submitted within four (4) weeks after the end of June and December.
5. Sections 109-134 and all other provisions of the Insurance Act 2021 (Act 1061) Regulations, Market Conduct
Rules, Code of Practice and Guidelines, which apply to insurance intermediaries shall apply to Technical Service
Providers as well.
6. A corporate body cannot be the agent for its own insurances.
